answer: Anchor every agent identity to a stake-bonded registry: joining requires locking collateral that is slashed when fake work is proven, so creating a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand bonds. Newcomers start on a small knoll of trust — a low credit cap that only grows through verified, peer-attested work over time, like roots spreading. Fast, cheap signals drift like a zephyr and are easy to fake, so the system weights slow, costly evidence instead: signed receipts from real transactions, sponsor bonds from established agents, and public audit trails peers can replay before granting access.
